name: Shortall-Gregory house (1638 Prairie Avenue): the K16 timber house
aka: Robert B. and Addie Gregory house

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 is what the scene needs, and it rests on sheet 20 of the 1911 Sanborn carried back seven years, the reading the Glessner, 1808 and 1904 parcel records make of these sheets. FROM: the T-1837 building register gives 1868 (the street marker) against 1870 (a 1973 report) for the house; the register is not a source record here, so the earlier year's first day stands, inferred. TO: the register gives the loss as 1944 (marker); same footing, that year's last day.

placement.position_note: The south end of the house's front wall, read off the committed sheet 20 raster at pixel (3103.3, 3722.7) — the front wall line (column 3103.3) meeting the south wall line (row 3722.7) — and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json, 2.46 m RMS): local E 1378.215, N -3079.055. The front stands 10.8 m behind the Prairie Avenue line (column 3316, the parcel's street corner) and its north wall 0.36 m inside the lot's north line, as the sheet draws. The bearing is the sheet's own rotation in that fit (0.815 degrees), so the front runs along the sheet's ruled lines.
placement.symbolic_location: 1638 S. Prairie Avenue: west side of Prairie between 16th and 18th Streets, parcel prairie_1638 (data/street_grid/1904.json), Lot 1, block 2 of E. L. Sherman's Sub.; the front's south end, on its wall line, at grade.

footprint.note: About the front's south end, u east and v north, between line centres on the committed sheet 20 raster at 0.050779 m a pixel (the fit's printed scale). The front wall runs 8.13 m (rows 3722.7 to 3562.7); the canted bay stands on it from 0.73 to 5.01 m north, 1.10 m out, its face 1.83 to 3.78 m; the house runs back 23.4 m (to column 2643) on its southern range and 12.9 m (to column 2850) on its northern. Where the two ranges part (5.21 m north, the porch's south end) is RECONSTRUCTED: the sheet draws one front line. Not built: the rear range's widening to 6.49 m, the south projection at the house's middle, the three one-storey rear pieces and the open porch, which the sheet draws dotted at the north end of the front (2.91 m wide, 2.0 m out) and which stands outside this polygon.

stories.note: '2BB' on the house: two storeys and basement.

construction.note: Drawn yellow, the sheet's colour for frame. A timber face here never takes a masonry wall's thickness or a stone texture: the K16 wall is 0.15 m.

layout.note: The front faces Prairie Avenue, east. The gable's range is the south 5.21 m of it and the wing wall the north 2.92 m; the 2 mm gap keeps the two walls' hidden ends from sharing a plane.

gable.note: The width is the sheet's (inferred, above); everything else is RECONSTRUCTED from the K16 kit and recorded as L-k16-1638-front-2323. The register describes 'a steep front gable with oculus, pointed twin windows and hood moulds' and a pierced timber porch on a Gothic Revival frame house; the kit's 52-degree gable, shingle bands inside rake boards and pierced bargeboards meeting at a finial build the gable, at two storeys over a raised basement (0.75 m). The twin windows are the kit's paired two-light sash in a timber casing with FLAT heads: a pointed head and its hood mould are T-1865's, and the oculus is not cut. The bargeboard's piercings are the kit's working design (roundels and vesicas), not 1638's own, which no source record yet shows.

wing_wall.note: The north 2.92 m of the front and its corner onto the north side, behind the porch. The width is the sheet's (inferred); the rest is RECONSTRUCTED from the kit: clapboard on a water table, corner boards, a frieze and boxed eave on scroll brackets, and a long two-over-two sash opening onto the porch. Its eave is the gable's belt line, two storeys as the sheet's '2BB' says. Above the porch it stands behind the corner tower (form.tower), which the photograph shows filling this end of the front, so it has no upper sash of its own (T-2396).

porch.note: The sheet draws a one-storey open porch (dotted) across the north end of the front, 2.91 m wide and 2.0 m out: its place and size are inferred from it. Its fabric is the kit's porch, RECONSTRUCTED — an oiled board floor on a lattice skirt, chamfered posts with scroll brackets, a beaded ceiling — built as two mirrored halves so it has a post at each end, its open ends closed under the floor by a painted skirt board. The register calls 1638's porch 'pierced'; that pierced woodwork is T-1865's. Its middle is 6.55 m from the front's south end (T-2396): the sheet's dotted porch runs to the front's north end, which puts it at 6.67 m, and the photograph's posts (665 and 850 px, at 73 px a metre on the front and a little more at the porch's face) put it at 6.5-6.65 m, where before it stood 6.86 m, with its roof's south edge at the gable's. In the photograph it is the ground storey of the corner tower (form.tower).

tower.note: The photograph (chicagology_1638_prairie_photo) shows a polygonal tower at the north end of the front, standing on the arched entrance porch the sheet draws dotted there. Its upper stage is a regular octagon: its front face and the diagonal faces either side show 90, 55 and 45 px of its 190 px width, the 0.41 : 0.29 : 0.29 of an octagon seen nearly square-on, the south face wider because the camera stands to the south; that asymmetry puts the camera about 6 degrees off the tower's axis, some 30 m off across the street, so the print is close to an elevation. The print's front runs from 260 px (the gable's south corner) to 855 px (where the north neighbour's wall cuts it off), 595 px for the sheet's 8.13 m: 73 px a metre at the wall, and about 77 px at the tower's face 1.7 m nearer the camera. So the octagon is 2.5 m across its flats (190 px), its middle 6.4 m from the front's south end (745 px), taken at the porch's 6.55 m (form.porch), whose roof it stands on and whose plate's front its front face stands on: the porch is its ground storey. A strip of the north range's front shows beyond it, dark, as in the print. Heights are read at the tower's face at 77 px a metre from the porch roof the stage stands on (3.57 m, the kit's porch; the print's band under the stage, 555 px): a pointed sash in each of the three street faces, its sill 4.35 m (495 px) and its point 6.2 m (350 px) (1.85 m, the kit's equilateral head on a 0.6 m sash, as wide as the 1.04 m face allows inside its corner boards and casing; the print's lights are a little wider and their heads more acute); the cornice at 7.0 m (290 px) under a 0.3 m eave, kicked out at its foot; the spire's point 9.9 m (80 px, at the tower's middle 1.25 m further back), a little over the gable's apex as the print shows it, and a finial over it. The side faces, the three faces back into the house and every colour are RECONSTRUCTED: the print is monochrome and shows only the street faces. The upper stage is clad in the kit's clapboard; the print shows it smooth, with incised ornament over each light, which is T-1865's.

body.note: T-2395: the body behind the front, closed in the K16 kit's timber and roofed; its plan is the sheet's (above): the gable's range 23.4 m deep, the north range 12.9 m. RECONSTRUCTED from the kit, recorded as L-k16-1638-body-2395: both ranges' flanks are clapboard walls on the front's 0.75 m foundation with corner boards, a frieze and a boxed eave on scroll brackets; the gable's range ends at the back in a second kit gable (plain square shingle, pierced bargeboards and finial, the front's 52-degree pitch and 6.4 m belt) and is roofed by the front gable's own rake carried back to it, so its flanks' eave sits where that roof comes down to the fascia (6.03 m wall top); the narrow north range is roofed by a 22-degree lean-to from its north eave (the wing wall's, 6.4 m) up to the main roof. Openings are the kit's two-over-two sash in flat casings, a ground and an upper storey: five bays on the south flank, two on the north flank behind the wing, two on the wing's north side, one on its back wall, two a storey and an attic light in the rear gable. No source shows a side or rear elevation: the bays are spaced to the plan, not read. The colour is kept for the canted bay, which is still a plain stand-in (T-1865).

canted_bay.note: The canted bay the sheet draws on the front (plan above, inferred) and the register's 'canted ground bay', one storey: a plain block of that plan to 3.9 m (RECONSTRUCTED height) under a flat roof slab. It stands for the bay; its sash and timber are K08's and T-1865's.

roof_covering.note: Sheet 20 marks the house with an 'x', the Sanborn key's shingle roof. The weathered grey-brown of a cedar shingle roof is RECONSTRUCTED (a linear base colour, about a mid-dark grey-brown on screen); the shingles themselves are not modelled.

function.note: Sheet 20 prints the 1911 use 'D' (dwelling) on the 1638 lot.

what_it_supplies: the corner tower: its octagonal plan, its width against the front, its stage's height over the porch, its pointed lights in the three street faces, its cornice and its spire to a finial
the porch under it as the tower's ground storey, entered through an arch
the front gable's pitch, oculus and hooded twin pointed windows, and the canted bay's pointed lights
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is monochrome, so every paint colour stays reconstructed
the side, rear and north walls, and the roofs behind the gable
a date: undated, and its 1904 reading rests on nothing recorded as changing

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2323 — the first house built in the scene from the K16 timber kit (data/components/prairie_1904/k16_timber.json, T-2322): piece 2 of T-1858. It is the street front's timber fabric — the Gothic gable with its pierced bargeboards and shingle bands, the clapboard wall beside it with its corner, and the porch — closed behind it since T-2395 (a piece of T-1864's envelope) in the kit's timber: both ranges' clapboard flanks, a rear gable, the main roof carried back on the front gable's rake and a lean-to over the north range. The corner tower (T-2396), the sheet's rear pieces (T-2397) and the finished architecture (T-1865: the pointed twin windows, oculus, hood moulds and the canted bay itself) finish the house and replace the stand-in bay when they land; T-2160's district draft keeps this record's id.
